evidence.note: Opening plan is recon-then-build: list dir, check existing code/deps, then 'write a compact Python web app' with sqlite3, endpoints, SSR UI, start.sh. Shows a foundations-first intent (durable storage) but stated as a flat list of subsystems, not milestones with done-checks.

Adopts stdlib+sqlite after finding no frameworks; plans one self-contained service covering OAuth, endpoints, seeded data, SSR, security headers, SSE — the whole surface enumerated but built as a single monolithic app.py write rather than sequenced increments.

Defensible ordering: py_compile → identify /oauth/authorize routing dependency → start server → validate health, hashes, UI, API. Verification is planned after the monolithic build rather than per-milestone.

Post-build hardening becomes a running remaining-work list (account registration, scope enforcement, poll voting, nodeinfo, CSRF fields, extra compat endpoints) — reactive punch-list, not dependency-aware milestones each with an explicit done-criterion.

reasoning: The agent shows a sensible coarse build order — recon, then durable storage/auth foundations, then endpoints/UI, then validation and hardening — and enumerates the major subsystems, which clears the flat-list-with-no-ordering bar of anchor 3. But there is no explicit milestone hierarchy with per-item verification hooks; subsystems are bundled into one monolithic write and remaining work surfaces as a reactive punch-list rather than sequenced, individually-verified increments, so it falls short of anchor 8. This best matches anchor 5: a defensible foundations-before-features plan with rough, mostly implicit done-criteria.
